note: Hand-written headers that SHADOW the generated tree. An override is placed earlier on the include path than the generated include directory, so the generated file stays untouched and the override is the whole of the modification: the set of files under overrides/include is the diff, and no computation is needed to find it. Reserved for what the declared mechanisms cannot reach -- source-patches/ rewrites the pinned TypeScript, repairs/ adds text with no behavior to emitted output, and either is preferable because neither carries a copy. An override does carry a copy, so each entry records `derivedFrom`, the sha256 of the generated file it was produced from. When a pin move changes that file the digest stops matching and `npm run overrides:check` says so, which is the signal to re-derive the override or drop it. Each entry also carries a `status`: `complete` means the override compiles, `incomplete` means it is partway and says what remains, so nobody mistakes a half-finished override for a finished one.

overrides.reason: After the localized initializer patch, the emitter still refuses cloneNumberBuffer because SequenceView erases the Array versus Float32Array carrier, cloneAnimationTrack, trimAnimationTrack, and validateAnimationTrack on nullable segment-easing tests, and sampleAnimationTrack on optional indexed easing projection. The retained helpers compile, but five public behaviors remain absent and five direct angle consumers call clone or sample.
overrides.change: Completes the emitted module with explicit optional handling for segment easings, source-equivalent keyframe cloning, trimming, validation, linear/step/cubic sampling, and quaternion normalization. SequenceView retains one additional observable fact—whether its erased numeric input was a Float32Array—so cloneNumberBuffer can allocate the backing type the source promises without exposing or copying the original buffer.
overrides.equivalence: Clones allocate independent time, value, and segment-easing storage while retaining easing callable identity and Float32Array versus Array backing. Sampling preserves boundary clamping, segment-first easing fallback, step, linear, Hermite cubic, shortest-arc quaternion slerp, and normalization. Trimming retains only in-range keyframes in source order, rebases time, slices the matching easing range, and always writes fresh Array buffers. Validation preserves diagnostic order, codes, indices, and the null-versus-array result. The retained initializer and helper bodies are unchanged.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A repair cannot add five behavioral functions. Local annotations can recover the initializer and might recover the optional easing expression, but ordinary TypeScript cannot restore the Array-versus-Float32Array carrier after the target has erased both into SequenceView; always cloning to one backing would change a documented public behavior. The runtime query is deliberately narrow and was checked against requires-based duck typing before addition.
overrides.unblocks: All five previously absent declarations compile. The partial generated animation_track.hpp already compiled by omitting them, so the direct compiled-header gain is +0. Across its five direct angle consumers in the current generated tree, animation_clip.hpp and animation_root_motion.hpp move from failing on the missing clone/sample declarations to compiling: +2 downstream headers, measured with unlimited diagnostics.
overrides.remaining: animation_crossfade.hpp advances past sampleAnimationTrack to an incompatible structural Array write; animation_blend_tree.hpp retains its independent readonly-row Array projection; contract.hpp cascades from blend tree and other independently failing modules. Those three do not count toward the measured gain.
